clues: This bird of prey has a name that may trace back to an ancient Latin word meaning simply 'hawk', with a French ending added on.
Bulkier and slower than a falcon, it soars in lazy circles hunting voles; in America, people often use its name for the vultures that circle over roadkill.
Calling a cranky old man an old one of these birds is a mild insult, and modern French still calls the bird a buse, from the same root.
